findings.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source, including Location.None. The requirement only asks to stop the crash. With FirstOrDefault() alone, diagnostics about members of a referenced type would still be reported at Location.None, which analyzers are allowed to do. The wrapper silently suppresses them, and any other TypeCollector diagnostic whose location helper returns null. README and MsgPack004.md now document that consumers never see these problems, which the requirement does not ask for.

questions.text: When a closed generic type from a referenced assembly has a member problem (for example a public member with no [Key], MsgPack004), should the consuming project still see a diagnostic?
options: No - drop it silently; the defining project reports it (what the change and the new docs do)
Yes - report it in the consumer at Location.None or on the consuming member, without crashing
questions.why_it_matters: With option 1 the ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter and the README/MsgPack004.md text are correct, and the low-severity finding is withdrawn. With option 2 the filter is a defect, because it hides real problems. The fix would then be only the FirstOrDefault/null-location changes, without wrapping reportDiagnostic, and the docs would be wrong.
